title: Mica powder burnish on polymer clay
subtitle: Rubbing mica powder onto raw polymer clay surfaces before curing for a metallic sheen
excerpt: Mica powder rubbed onto raw polymer clay before curing gives a bright, almost metallic surface that bonds permanently during the cure. The technique is quick and low-cost compared to painting after curing. It works on any raw polymer clay surface, from flat tiles to sculpted forms.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from established polymer clay surface methods.

glossaryTerms.definition: A fine mineral powder with light-reflective particles that gives surfaces a pearlescent or metallic sheen

content.text: applied to raw polymer clay bonds into the surface as it hardens. It gives a metallic sheen with no sealing needed. The technique takes under five minutes and works on any polymer clay.

materials.name: Raw polymer clay piece (shaped but not yet cured)
Mica powder, gold, bronze, or silver

content.text: Shape and smooth the polymer clay piece as usual. Do not cure it yet.

Dip the dry liner brush lightly into the mica powder. Tap off excess. Brush over the surface of the raw clay in gentle circular strokes. The natural tackiness of the unbaked clay picks up and holds the powder.
Build up coverage in several light passes rather than loading heavy powder at once, which can obscure surface texture.
For edge highlights: brush mica powder onto the raised edges and tips of a textured surface. Leave the recesses plain to create contrast.
Cure at 130°C for the time appropriate to the piece thickness. Ventilate the kitchen. After curing, the mica powder is locked into the surface permanently. No extra sealer is required.

Use two powder colours on one piece: apply a darker base powder first, then dab a lighter or different-coloured powder to raised areas only for a two-tone effect. Mix powders on the brush to create an intermediate colour.

items.problem: Powder appears dull and grey rather than metallic after curing
items.cause: The mica powder was loaded too heavily or the clay surface was dusty before application
items.fix: Buff the cured surface briskly with a soft cloth or fingertip to bring out the reflective quality. Heavy overloading of powder can dull the effect

items.cause: The surface may have been contaminated with hand cream or talc, preventing proper bonding
items.fix: Apply a thin coat of liquid polymer clay medium or clay-compatible varnish over the cured piece to lock the powder in place
